observations: Reviewer task ID: none was supplied by the runtime, so task is null.

What I read: I opened storyboards-unnumbered/page-05.png, storyboards/page-05.png and review/page-05.png with Read and looked at them. All were readable. I read the full page plan and the first reading.

05-1: Meera is left and Ravi right, with Ravi's dark-blue phone between them and Meera's finger pointing at it. In the art this gives Welbuk Health the visual anchor that first-reading issue (b) found missing. The monitor and the waiting chairs set the scene back at reception.

05-2: Ravi holds the phone toward the reader, showing abstract calendar and heart cards. This shows 'useful information in one place' before he asks. The balloon tail is short but goes to his face, and the WELBUK HEALTH label at bottom-left is read after the balloon.

05-3: Meera is left, facing right, with Ravi's shoulder and phone in the right foreground. This keeps the 05-1 axis. Same caveat as 03-2: waiting chairs with patients appear behind Meera. I refer this to the artwork review. It does not break the reading.

05-4: outside the clinic, Ananya and Meera wave from the glass doorway at left, and Ravi walks right, waving, with bag and phone. The walkthrough Meera offers in 05-3 is implied by the cut to the reassured departure and the 'smoother visit' caption. That matches the source's four beats. Ananya's appearance at the door is a natural farewell and needs no setup (first-reading issue (d)).

Without guides: Meera's balloon (top-left), then Ravi's question (middle-left) and the teal label below it, then Meera's answer (middle-right), then the departure caption across the top of the last panel.
The question in 05-2 and the answer in 05-3 sit side by side in the same row, so the reply comes right after the question. Ravi's exit to the right in 05-4 leads toward the page turn.

transitions.observation: The consultation room changes to the reception desk: monitor, keyboard, waiting chairs, and the bag back on Ravi's shoulder. Same visit, after the consultation.
We cut in to the phone Meera was pointing at. Ravi now holds it in both hands with the screen toward us, and the same waiting area is behind him.
Reverse to Meera answering. Ravi's shoulder and phone are in the right foreground and she gestures toward the phone, the same object.
Time skip to his departure, outside the entrance. Ananya and Meera are in the doorway, and Ravi carries the same bag and phone. The caption sums up the visit.

Ravi walks away to the right and the next panel finds him in a train seat with the same shirt, bag and phone. The caption 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown' marks it as a possible future trip.

readingReview.comparison: Same order as the first reading. Issue (a), the setting change, is carried by the reception set. Issue (b), no device, is resolved by the phone in 05-1 to 05-3. Issue (c), the unseen walkthrough, is an acceptable ellipsis that the caption resolves. Issue (d), Ananya without setup, works as a farewell. Issue (e), Ravi right throughout, is confirmed.
